en: One Scroll of the *Vajraśekhara-sūtra: The Method for Cultivating the Practice of the Tathāgata Avalokiteśvararāja*.
Compiled by the Grand Master of the Household, Peer of the State, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, Duke of Sui.

The Śramaṇa Amoghavajra, Tripitaka Master of Daixingshan Monastery, who was granted a fief of three thousand households, invested with the rank of Purple Robe, posthumously honored as Minister of Works, and bestowed the title of Great Mirror, Great Universal Wisdom—herein respectfully translates by imperial decree, relying upon the *Vajraśekhara Sūtra*: "I now, in accordance with the *Vajraśekhara Sūtra*..."
To expound the essential Dharma of the Vajra Lotus,
one must first enter the consecration Samaya Maṇḍala and generate the great bodhicitta.
They sacrifice their bodies, lives, and wealth to benefit all beings;
they are courageous and diligent, remaining in accord with mindfulness;
and their loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity are uninterrupted.
Only such a person as this should practice it.
The methods for drawing the maṇḍala, its images, and so forth, are as extensively described in other sūtras.
Whenever one enters a vihāra intending to perform recitation, [one should proceed as follows].
First, place the five limbs upon the ground and prostrate to the Honored One, the Tathāgata Avalokiteśvararāja. Next,
pay homage to the Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi of the north, and so forth, up to the Tathāgatas Akṣobhya, Ratnasaṃbhava, and Vairocana.
All together, according to the Dharma, they pay homage with utmost sincerity and reverence.
Kneeling on both knees with palms joined in the lotus gesture,
they repent for all transgressions of the three karmas.
Throughout immeasurable kalpas, I have been adrift in the ocean of birth and death;
now, with a pure mind, I reveal and repent my transgressions,
just as all Buddhas have repented, so do I now likewise.
May I and all sentient beings be completely purified.
The mantra is:
Oṃ svabhāva-śuddhāḥ sarva-dharmāḥ svabhāva-śuddho ’ham. One should then rejoice in the merit and wisdom accumulated by all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the past, present, and future.
The roots of goodness accumulated by the Buddhas of the three times past, as well as by bodhisattvas and sentient beings— joining my palms, I rejoice in them all.
Next, one should place the right knee upon the ground.
With an open mind, join your palms and place them upon the crown of your head.
Visualize that you are prostrating at the feet of all the Buddhas, Tathāgatas, and Bodhisattvas.
Recite the secret mantra as follows:
Having paid homage to all the Buddhas by reciting "Oṃ padmavitta" (the syllable *tta* being a half-syllable joined with *vi*),
one sits according to the seat-mudrā and enters meditative absorption through contemplation.
Visualize immeasurable Tathāgatas pervading the entire dharma-realm,
with the practitioner’s own body present within all those assemblies.
Then, bind the secret samaya-mudrā.
Firmly bind with the wisdom of *dāna*, *prajñā*, *dhyāna*, and *jñāna*;
joining them together, hold them upright,
and thereby awaken the assembly of noble ones.
Recite the secret mantra:
Oṃ vajrapadma samayas tvaṃ. Then, one should form the Samaya-mudrā that pleases and delights all Tathāgatas.
Following the previous mudrā, place only the *kṣamā* (ring finger) and *anāmikā* (pinky) fingers into the palms.
The mantra is: Oṃ samaya hūḥ surata siddhyaṃ. Then, perform the Heart Mudrā (*hṛdaya-mudrā*).
Visualize the syllable *traḥ* upon each of the two breasts;
with the vajra-bind,
strike them three times to open them.
The mantra is:
Oṃ vajra bandha traṭ. Then, one forms the seal of the entry of the wisdom-syllable before oneself.
Visualize the syllable *sa* upon a single red lotus flower;
enter its center with the meditative wisdom of the firm bond,
maintaining the balance between the forward and upward forces.
Visualize grasping those syllables within your heart and recite the secret mantra:
Oṃ vajrāveśa āḥ. Then, perform the seal of the *jñāna* syllable.
Without changing the previous mudrā,
extend the forceful fingers (anāmikā) to support the backs of the dhyāna and wisdom fingers (madhyamā),
visualizing the closing of the gate of the heart.
The mantra is: Oṃ vajramuṣṭi khaṃ.
Next, perform the mudrā for warding off obstacles and binding the boundary (*rakṣā-sīmābandha*):
interlace the fingers with the right hand pressing over the left, with the palms facing outward.
Patience and Vow support one another;
with the Hook of Exertion and the Square of Precepts,
and with the Thumb and Forefinger of Meditation and Wisdom, they grasp the Head of Generosity and Insight.
The mantra is:
Oṃ āmlīṣṭa-nābha-vau hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ (the *phaṭ* is pronounced with a single-syllable intonation). With this mudrā, rotate three times to the left.
Expel all that is unwholesome.
Circumambulate three times to the right,
establishing a boundary (sīmā) at whatever distance one desires.
Next, form the Samādhi Mudrā:
with both hands facing upward and crossed,
extend the index fingers and the thumbs so that they face each other and stand upright.
Holding the *dhyāna* and *prajñā* mudrās with the thumbs and forefingers,
place them upon the crossed legs and recite the secret mantra as follows:
Oṃ samādhi padma hrīḥ. Clearly perceiving each inhalation and exhalation of the breath, one visualizes immeasurable Buddhas within the expanse of space.
At that time, he snapped his fingers to alert the practitioner and addressed him, saying:
"How can you hope to attain unexcelled enlightenment now,
when you do not know the essential dharma of the true reality of all Buddhas?"
At that time, having heard the exhortation, the practitioner addressed the Buddha, saying: "What is called 'the reality' (tattva)?
I pray only that the Tathāgata will explain it for me."
At that time, the Buddhas said to the practitioner:
"Excellent, excellent! You are able to ask such a question.
Visualize the syllable 'evil' (akṣara) within your heart, making it translucent throughout the mind."
Recite the mantra:
Oṃ jita-pratiti-viṃdga-lu-mi. Recite this silently once, and then visualize it as a lunar disc (candramaṇḍala).
As if in a light mist,
in order to cause the lunar disc to become pure,
one recites this secret mantra:
Oṃ bodhicittam utpādayāmi. Having recited this, contemplate the moon at the heart, making it utterly pure, like the vast expanse of the great sky, free from all blemish or obscuration.
Furthermore, one should visualize a lotus flower within the moon of the mind.
Recite the mantra:
Oṃ tiṣṭha vajra padma. One should then contemplate that lotus as being identical to the moon.
Gradually extending it until it pervades the entire *dharmadhātu*,
equal in measure to empty space,
one recites the secret mantra as follows:
Oṃ sarvavajrapadma. From within the lotus, immeasurable light is emitted.
Following the light, there flow forth infinite and boundless worlds of Sukhāvatī;
each world is adorned with exquisite jewels,
and in every one resides the Tathāgata Avalokiteśvararāja.
Surrounded by the assembly of noble ones in front and behind,
having visualized thus, he gradually withdraws the lotus flower and recites the secret mantra as follows:
Oṃ saṃhara padma. Thus, all the Buddhas and Tathāgatas of all worlds gather [the flowers] according to the petals, their size equal to their own bodies.
He immediately transformed his own body into the form of Amitāyus Buddha,
the color of red crystal, emitting great radiance,
and sat upon a vajra-lotus throne while forming the samādhi mudrā.
Having visualized oneself as the Tathāgata,
one should further fear distraction and subsequent regression; therefore,
one next performs the empowerment seal (adhiṣṭhāna-mudrā) to empower [the visualization].
Firmly bind with the power of progress, bending like a lotus petal.
With the dhyāna and wisdom fingers held upright, seal the heart, forehead, throat, and crown of the head as appropriate.
Visualize the syllable *Hrīḥ*.
Recite the secret mantra:
Oṃ vajradharma hrīḥ. Next, form the consecration mudrā:
join the palms in the lotus gesture, with the index fingers and thumbs pressed together like a jewel.
Holding the thumb and index finger upright and far apart,
place them upon the forehead and recite the secret mantra:
Oṃ padmaratna viśeṣa sarvaman hṛt. Next, form the mudrā of the lotus garland.
First, the mudrā proceeds from the forehead to the hands,
circles back to behind the crown of the head,
and then forms the lotus fist.
In the manner of a bound flower garland, slowly descend forward and recite the secret mantra:
Oṃ padma-ratna-male maṃ. Then, perform the armor-seal (*kavaca-mudrā*).
Form the Lotus Fist mudrā and encircle the body from front to back as if donning armor,
reciting the secret mantra as follows:
Oṃ (1) abhaya (2) padma (3) kavace (4) bandha (5) rakṣa me (6) hūṃ (7) haṃ (8). Next, form the mudrā of joy.
With lotus-like palms joined, gently clap them three times and recite the mantra:
Oṃ padmaduḥkha-hūṃ. Then, once again before one’s face...
Visualize the world of Sukhāvatī,
with its ground of lapis lazuli and its ocean of meritorious milk;
within that ocean, visualize the syllable *hrīḥ*.
It transforms into a subtle, blossoming lotus flower,
which then transforms into the Tathāgata Avalokiteśvararāja,
adorned with physical marks and features as previously described for the body-vision.
Next, bind the Lotus Hook Mudrā.
Join the palms in the lotus gesture, with the forefingers curved like hooks.
Recite the mantra as follows:
Oṃ padmaṃ huṃ jaḥ. Then, form the lotus-noose mudrā by interlacing the index and middle fingers like a ring as with the previous mudrā.
Recite the secret mantra:
Oṃ padmamoghapāśa hūṃ. Fourth, form the Lotus Chain Seal (*padma-śṛṅkhalā-mudrā*):
join the palms like a lotus bud and interlace the thumbs and ring fingers in the gesture of meditative concentration.
The powers and wisdoms are likewise;
they interlock to form a chain.
Recite the secret mantra as follows:
Oṃ padma saṃbhūta maṃ. Then, form the lotus-bell mudrā: join the palms in the lotus gesture;
place the *dhyāna* and *jñāna* fingers (the thumbs) inside, while the *vajra* and *bala* fingers (the index and middle fingers) are joined like a ring.
Recite the secret mantra:
Oṃ padma-vaiśvānara hūṃ. Then recite the hundred-syllable mantra of the Lotus Family (*padmakula*).
Holding the argha vessel, [proceed].
One should offer worship with perfumed water blended with saffron and camphor,
reciting the hundred-syllable mantra as follows:
Oṃ *pramādasaṃyamanupālaya pramadasattvatevinubodhiṣṭha nirdhuta-maṃjava.
Sudhārasa-mṛdvīkā (10) Anurakta-mṛdvīkā (11) Subhāṣita-mṛdvīkā (12) Sarvasiddhim-prayaccha (13) Sarvakarma-sujaya (14) Cintāśrī... (15)
15. *saṃyoga* (combine the medicines), 16. *julu*, 17. *hūṃ*, 18.
*sarvatathāgata*, 25. *praṇama*, 26. *maṅgalaṃ ca*, 27. *praṇama*.
27. *Māṃ* (two syllables), *pava*; 28. *mahāsamaya*; 29. *sattva*; 30. *aḥ*.
Next, form the Lotus Inner Four Offerings Play Mudrā.
With the hands joined like lotus petals, raise both the wisdom and action fingers together while reciting the secret mantra:
Oṃ padma-rāśi hūḥ. Next, perform the mudrā of the lotus garland.
Then, with the same mudrā,
extend both arms and recite the mantra as follows:
Oṃ padma-male traḥ. Next, form the Lotus Gāndhārī mudrā by joining the palms like a lotus flower.
They bend and support the various *pāramitās*,
rising from the navel to the mouth before dispersing.
Recite the secret mantra:
Oṃ padma nṛtye nṛtya. Then, form the lotus dance mudrā.
Joining the palms like a lotus flower,
rotate them to the left and right,
and scatter them above the crown of the head.
Recite the secret mantra:
Oṃ padma nirdiṣṭa kṛta. (4) Form the mudrā for burning incense as the fourth outer offering of the lotus.
The lotus and palms are lowered and scattered,
like burning incense.
Recite the secret mantra as follows:
Oṃ padma dūpe hūṃ. Next, perform the mudrā for scattering lotus flowers:
join the palms in the lotus gesture and scatter them upward in front.
It is like the power of scattering flowers.
Recite the mantra:
Oṃ padma puṣpe oṃ. Then, form the lotus-lamp mudrā.
With the hands joined in the lotus *añjali* mudrā, the thumbs (*jñāna*) and index fingers (*citta*) are pressed closely together.
Recite the mantra: Oṃ padma-nibhi ni. Then, form the lotus *vilepana* (scented unguent) mudrā.
Ten times, perform the lotus *añjali* gesture at the heart,
then open the hands as if spreading [incense],
in the manner of anointing with fragrant unguents (*vilepana*).
Recite the secret mantra:
Oṃ padma kṣiti-ṇe. Then, firmly bind the root mudrā, joining the thumbs and ring fingers together.
It is in the shape of a lotus leaf.
Recite the mantra:
Oṃ ekalokeśvara rājā hili. This forms the root mudrā.
Having recited the vidyā seven times,
one should then take up the lotus-seed rosary and perform the recitation with the appropriate visualization.
Perform this according to one's capacity throughout the four periods of the day.
When wishing to conclude,
re-bind the root mudrā and recite the root dhāraṇī seven times.
Next, bind the mudrās of the eight offerings.
Then, dismiss the Honored One using the dismissal mudrā.
First, perform the root mudrā:
extend the hands from the navel up to the face and then spread them out,
joining the palms above the crown of the head.
Visualize that the Tathāgata Avalokiteśvararāja returns to his original palace.
Recite the mantra:
Oṃ vajrapadma muḥ. Having thus dispatched the deity, [proceed].
Make aspirations as you wish.
Then, protect the body with the *kavaca-mudrā* (armor seal) and establish the boundary with the *Hayagrīva-vajra-pāśa-mudrā* (the seal of the Hayagrīva Vidyārāja).
Circumambulate counter-clockwise to dissolve the ritual boundaries. Walk at will through various pure locations,
reading Mahāyāna sūtras such as the Mahāprajñāpāramitā, the Avataṃsaka, the Nirvāṇa, and the Laṅkāvatāra.
Whether walking, standing, sitting, or reclining, one should constantly maintain mindfulness of the Honored One without interruption.
This is the *Vajraśekhara-sūtra* method for the practice of the Tathāgata Avalokiteśvararāja.
